rule: Objective-C grammar provenance: wired bytes vs a rebuild of the committed patched source vs pristine upstream
why: objc runs a PATCHED vendored grammar and was one of 21 UNPINNED lanes, which is the worst case for a pin: the pin exists to catch 'the wired bytes are not a build of the source we think they are', and a patched grammar is exactly where that happens — grammar.js is edited, rebuilt, and nothing downstream notices. Identity is claimed on SURFACE and BEHAVIOUR, never on bytes, because a wasm build carries its emscripten version, compiler flags and section order.

rebuild.of: a fresh build of the committed patched source in grammars/tree-sitter-objc

byteIdentity.note: expected false for both, and the reason identity is claimed on surface/behaviour instead

patchEvidence.patchAddsDerivedFrom: the wired-vs-pristine named-surface diff, so a hand-written list cannot report a rule as a missing node type

verdict: HONEST: the wired bytes are a build of the committed patched source (surface identical in both directions, analyzer output identical on all 329 routed files), and the patches are live (8 node types present in WIRED and all absent from pristine, zero the other way; 1 added RULES have no node type by design — macro_enum_specifier). Pristine is worse on the corpus: 622 ERROR nodes vs 158 for WIRED, 4779 vs 5095 symbols, 23754 vs 24226 relationships.
